newsitem.title: FRANCE: France steps up anti-terror watch.
newsitem.headline: France steps up anti-terror watch.

text.p: France sharply increased security in the Paris area on Friday, adding an extra 1,000 men to the 2,000 soldiers and riot police patrolling rail stations, public transport and airports since a December 3 commuter train blast, Interior Minister Jean-Louis Debre said.
"We are in a difficult period. The situation abroad is not good," Debre told reporters.

He did not specify to which country he was referring but did say the precautions were also taken because of the Thursday sentencing in Paris of a group of Moslem fundamentalists held responsible for backing attacks in Morocco.
Debre also said the start of the Moslem fast period of Ramadan was reason to be on alert.

Intelligence sources said French security services were also warned to be vigilant around Saturday's fifth anniversary of the military intervention in Algeria which put an end to general elections which Islamic fundamentalists were poised to win.

French authorities have already said they suspected the December 3 bombing, which killed four people and wounded nearly 100, was the work of Algerian Islamists who claimed responsibility for a previous wave of attacks in Paris in 1995.

Among forces boosting the security forces is a contingent of some 320 soldiers from the famed French Foreign Legion whose last experience in a police operation was in the bloody 1956-1957 Battle of Algiers in the former French territory.
But the legionnaires now patrolling the Paris metro (underground railway) are there to back up police and have no powers of arrest themselves.
